newsitem.title: SPAIN: Telefonica unruffled by EU cable deal ban.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica unruffled by EU cable deal ban.

text.p: Telefonica shares traded marginally lower in Madrid on Thursday, unruffled by a statement from European Union Commissioner Karel Van Miert saying he wanted to ban its cable television deal with Canal Plus.
Telefonica was quoted 10 pesetas lower at 2,635 pesetas at 1404 gmt.

Traders ignored Wednesday's reports from EU sources that Telefonica would pull out of Cablevision rather than face the ruling. Telefonica, which has so far refused to comment on the issue, maintained its silence.
"Telefonica is not going to make any public statement, either on the Commissioner's decision or on reports that we plan to abandon Cablevision," a spokesman told Reuters.
Some analysts said that even if the partly state-owned telecoms operator pulled out of the venture, the repercussions would be small.

"It's not great news," said Chris McFadden, telecoms analyst at Merrill Lynch in London. "Is it desperately bad news? Probably not. It's a bit of a setback but I don't think it makes a fundamental difference to the company."

Telefonica has risen in recent sessions after dropping to 2,545 pesetas on November 4 from 2,650 on October 28. Sentiment was dampened by Goldman Sachs's decision on October 29 to downgrade the company to market outperform from a trading buy.
